claim: The bound AMR-Hub code example at commit 4f3f6c32872c4b0a1486b47f82c8272c34f70db5 documents a configurable DXF-to-room-geometry method. The extractor reads a DXF-derived GeoDataFrame with a Layer column, polygonises configured room-boundary linework, filters point room labels by configured label layer/floor prefix, applies configured polygon corrections, optionally normalises shared wall faces to a midline, and projects configured door-layer linework grouped by EntityHandle onto room boundaries. The example configuration names ROOM_BOUNDARIES and ROOM_LABELS as polygon and label layers and Internal doors as a door layer; these are example configuration values, not universal layer names. The resulting room polygons are serialised to YAML with zero-thickness wall and door line segments; CAD door swing/leaf geometry is not retained in that YAML. The code assumes indoor local Cartesian coordinates and no CRS, and performs topological operations. It does not identify the source coordinate units, metric scale, georeferencing or a transform. These planar source coordinates are not asserted to be metric coordinates or RFC 7946 GeoJSON coordinates; no GeoJSON conversion is documented in the bounded paths. This is software-method evidence only. No real ED CAD/layout, as-operated capacity, verified connectivity or traversability, accessible route, manual annotation, operational or clinical review, or usable route graph is established. The root LICENSE snapshot identifies the MIT License and UCL-ARC copyright; its exact bytes are separately hash-bound below.
